Q1: The suggested fix touches `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py`, which is outside this issue's scope marker. How should the fix be scoped?
Choices:
A) Stay inside the current scope. Change only `scripts/ai_engine_fallback_report.sh` (and if needed `scripts/ai_engine.sh` / `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh`) so the consumer run's log gets a structured line with the pool step's reason (for example `pool_reason=<token>`, read with the same symlink, 64-byte and `[a-z0-9_]{1,60}` rules as `ai_engine_no_account_reason`). Add a regression test under `tests/`. The heal payload, `no_credential`, the record format and the fingerprint stay unchanged. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Widen the scope to the full suggested fix. Also change `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py`: an optional `--pool-reason` on `build-engine-fallback-payload`, a `Claude pool step reason:` evidence line, and `validate-payload` filtering. This needs an operator to re-file or re-scope the issue, because the pipeline cannot widen a verified scope marker (an edit to it makes `verify_heal_scope` report `edited`).
C) Do both. Ship A now on this issue, and open a separate follow-up issue for the `workflow_failure_heal.py` payload change.
D) Make no code change. Treat this as an operator-only check (read the "Resolve Claude credential" step log of run 40951784257, then `/reclarify`) and close the issue.
**Note:** B and C's follow-up both need an operator to act on the scope. Choosing B on this issue as it stands will stop again at the plan gate.
